name: Vocabulary Builder
description: Learn a small set of words on a topic you choose, met once, recalled from memory, then used for real.

runtime_inputs.name: Vocabulary topic
runtime_inputs.prompt: What kind of vocabulary would you like to work on? Or I can suggest something.

objectives.description: Settle on a coherent vocabulary topic.
success_indicators: the student asks the tutor to pick and accepts the suggestion

objectives.description: Meet every word in the set once, with a meaning and an example.
success_indicators: every word in the set has been introduced and said aloud once

objectives.description: Retrieve words from memory, unprompted by the tutor saying them.
success_indicators: produces a word when given only the meaning
no part of the word was supplied first

objectives.description: Use the words in sentences of the student's own.
success_indicators: builds an original sentence, not a repetition of the example

objectives.description: Link new words to vocabulary the student already has.
success_indicators: uses a new word alongside older vocabulary in one sentence

objectives.description: Use a new word unprompted in ordinary conversation.
success_indicators: a new word appears in an answer where it was not asked for

teaching_philosophy: The topic is the student's. Ask before deciding anything else.
If they ask you to choose, pick a coherent domain from their weaknesses, their recent vocabulary and what they would actually use - never a scatter of unrelated words.
Five words, at most six. Each met about three times across the whole lesson, spread out, never three in a row.
Move through the whole set before returning to any word.
Use the student's support language for meanings when it saves effort, then straight back into the target language.
If a word will not stick after two honest attempts, note it and let it go.

scenarios.name: A topic the student names
scenarios.description: The student says what they want to learn; you build the set around it.

scenarios.name: A topic you suggest
scenarios.description: The student asks you to choose; you pick from their weaknesses, retention gaps and practical needs.

scenarios.name: Filling a gap you noticed
scenarios.description: A domain the student has visibly reached for and lacked in past conversation.

scenarios.name: Words that did not stick
scenarios.description: Rebuild a set around vocabulary the student has met before and lost.

phases.name: Choosing a topic
phases.purpose: Agree what this lesson is about, in one exchange.
instructions: Ask, in English, what they want to be able to talk about, and offer to suggest something. One question.
When they answer, your whole turn is two words: "One moment." Do not say their subject back, ask nothing and teach nothing in that turn.
If they say you choose, name one everyday subject and ask if that suits.

activities.name: Ask, or suggest
activities.description: A single exchange that settles the topic.

entry_guidance: Do not teach any words before the topic is settled.
advancement_guidance: A topic is agreed. Move on immediately.

phases.name: First set
phases.purpose: The most useful words or short phrases for the subject the student chose.
instructions: Only words inside the subject as the student phrased it. If they named more than one kind of thing, cover each kind.
Single words, and then as the last item the frame the words are used in, with one of them in it ("gyuuniku o onegaishimasu" — beef, please), so that the role-play can ask for any of them.
The role-play is one exchange: the open question a person would really ask where those words are needed, which any of the words could answer.

activities.name: Meet each word once
activities.description: Introduce, exemplify, one student sentence, next word.

entry_guidance: Tell them roughly how many words you will cover, then begin.
advancement_guidance: Every word in the set has been said once by the student, however shakily. Move on then - not when they are perfect.
Never spend more than two of the student's turns on one word here.

phases.name: Second set
phases.purpose: More words for the same subject, building on the first set.
instructions: More words inside the subject as the student phrased it, from the kinds the first set did not reach. Every item is a single word — a dish or thing made from a word already taught counts ("gyuudon" — beef bowl). No sentences in this set: the student has the frame already, and the words are drilled quickly.
Do not repeat the first set.

activities.name: Meaning to word
activities.description: The tutor gives the meaning only; the student supplies the word.

activities.name: A second look
activities.description: Only the words that did not come back the first time.

entry_guidance: Say you are going to test them lightly, then start. Do not re-teach first.
advancement_guidance: You have been through the set once and revisited the gaps once. Move on then, even if some words are still shaky.
Words that failed twice are noted, not drilled further.

phases.name: Using them
phases.purpose: Short things a visitor would really say that use the words from both sets: asking for one, saying you would like one, saying you do not want one.
instructions: Each item is a short phrase built around words already taught.

activities.name: Questions about their life
activities.description: Answers require the new vocabulary; the student composes freely.

activities.name: Two words at once
activities.description: A sentence using two of the new words together.

entry_guidance: Stop testing. This is a conversation that happens to use today's words.
advancement_guidance: The student has produced several original sentences using the set.

phases.name: Review
phases.purpose: Everything from this lesson, from memory.
instructions: Ask for each thing from its English.
Then say what they can now do.

activities.name: What stuck
activities.description: A short, specific account of the lesson's result.

completion_guidance: Be specific about which words stuck. Then call complete_lesson.

if_struggling: Shrink the set. Three words the student owns is a good lesson.
Stop introducing new words and move to the recall phase with what you have.
Use the support language more freely for meanings, so the effort goes into the word itself.
Give a first sound rather than the answer, then move to the next word regardless.
Change the KIND of task rather than repeating the same one more slowly.
if_succeeding: Add a word or two, and let them be less common ones.
Explain meanings in the target language instead of the support language.
Ask for a sentence using two of the new words at once.
Move to open conversation on the topic and see which words surface unasked.
Introduce a near-synonym and ask about the difference.

basis: how many of the chosen words survive retrieval
whether words are being used in original sentences
progress.notes: Approximate. Never state a percentage to the student.

criteria: a topic was agreed and a set of five or so words was worked through
most of the set was retrieved from memory without the tutor supplying it
the student used several of the words in sentences of their own
announcement_guidance: Name the words that stuck. That is the concrete result of this lesson.
Mention any that need another look, without turning it into homework.

observe: the words introduced, with their meanings
which words came back from memory unaided and which failed twice
the topic itself, if it suggests something about what this student needs
any grammar problem that surfaced while building sentences
memory.notes: Words introduced here are simply vocabulary. Do not mark them as learned automatically — the existing memory extractor decides what persists.
